name: How Do Bathroom Waterproofing Failures Happen?

mainEntity.name: How do bathroom waterproofing failures usually happen during a remodel?
mainEntity.text: How do bathroom waterproofing failures usually happen during a remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom waterproofing failures are often caused by shortcuts at the most important hidden layers of the remodel. If the substrate is not prepared correctly, if waterproof membranes are installed inconsistently, or if shower pans and drain details are not completed properly, water can slowly penetrate the structure. Corners, niches, curbs, and transitions are especially vulnerable. A bathroom may look finished and still be leaking behind the walls. Homeowners should ask the contractor which waterproofing system will be used, who installs it, and how it is inspected before tile begins. Because repairs after the fact can be expensive, waterproofing should be treated as one of the most important quality-control items in the entire project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Waterproofing failures usually come from poor substrate prep, missing membrane coverage, bad shower pan detailing, rushed tile installation, or incorrect transitions at drains and corners. Small mistakes can allow water to reach framing and subfloors over time. Proper waterproofing should be treated as a system, not just a finish step.
